_sources.sea_level_temperature: North 1975, J. Atmos. Sci. 32:2033; North, Cahalan & Coakley 1981, Rev. Geophys. 19:91: annual zonal-mean surface temperature from the energy-balance model, fitted to observations as T(phi) = T0 + T2 P2(sin phi), T0 = 14.97 C, T2 = -28.0 C.
_sources.seasonal_amplitude: North & Coakley 1979, J. Atmos. Sci. 36:1189 seasonal EBM: the annual cycle amplitude grows ~ sin(phi). Half-range at the pole taken as 15.5 K (Northern Hemisphere zonal mean) [verify]. Mean of the warm half of a sinusoidal year = annual mean + (2/pi) x amplitude.
_sources.lapse_rate: U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 (NOAA/NASA/USAF, NOAA-S/T 76-1562): troposphere lapse rate 6.5 K/km.
_sources.tree_line: Koerner & Paulsen 2004, J. Biogeogr. 31:713: worldwide the alpine tree line sits where the growing-season mean root-zone temperature is 6.4 +- 0.7 C.
_sources.ice_line: Equilibrium-line proxy: permanent snow/ice where even the warm-season mean stays below 0 C (no net melt season); Ohmura, Kasser & Funk 1992, J. Glaciol. 38:397 (ELA summer temperature near 0 C at low precipitation).
_sources.continentality: Seasonal amplitude over land vs ocean comes from the simulation's own first-order column response (climate_seed::damped_seed: amplitude 1/sqrt(1+(w tau)^2), tau = C/(B + C_tr), land and ocean heat capacities in surface/heat_capacity.rs). The 15.5 K pole half-range is a zonal mean over a band that is about 70% land at 60-70 N [verify], so a site's amplitude is that half-range times (its own land/ocean damping mix) / (the band's mix). Its own mix uses climate_seed::maritime_weight (exp(-coast distance / L)).
_sources.zone_season: Tree and ice lines use the mean of the warmest quarter of the year (fraction 0.25), not the warm half: Ohmura et al. 1992 relate the ELA to the June-August (3-month) mean, and at alpine tree lines the Koerner & Paulsen 2004 growing season is about 3 months. Mean of the warmest fraction f of a sinusoidal year = annual mean + amplitude x sin(pi f)/(pi f) (f = 0.5 gives 2/pi).
